items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: the day I started Cyndi Lauper was doing her debut record in Studio B

ctx.x: We were talking about, sort of that entrance into —

Yeah. I mean it was exciting at Record Plant from the day I walked in there. Because there were four studios plus two remote trucks at Record Plant. So they were always doing something with the top people, like if you walked in the door, on the ground floor to the left was Studio B and the day I started Cyndi Lauper was doing her debut record in Studio B; J. Geils Band was up in the mix room doing the “Freeze Frame” album, which was like their multi-platinum hit; I think Willie Nile was in another room; you’d…
the next day I could do it, because I have so much technical background, that tech stuff was cake for me.
